concepts.title: A Torchlight: Source of the Idea
concepts.definition: Opening a torch shows the essentials of an electric circuit in miniature: cells that push the current, a bulb that glows, and metal strips that join them into one closed path.
concepts.key_idea: A torch is a circuit you can hold: current, source and path together make light.

concepts.title: A Simple Electrical Circuit
concepts.definition: Join a cell, wires and a bulb into a closed loop and the bulb glows: this complete, unbroken path is a closed circuit; a gap anywhere, an open circuit, stops the current and the light.
concepts.formula: closed circuit = cell + wires + bulb joined end to end
concepts.key_idea: Current flows only in a closed loop: one break, one glowless bulb.

concepts.title: Circuit Diagrams and Symbols
concepts.definition: Electricians shorten circuits to paper: standard symbols for cell, bulb, wire and switch let anyone draw a circuit diagram that another person anywhere can rebuild exactly.
concepts.key_idea: Symbols are the grammar of circuits: a neat diagram carries the whole design.

concepts.title: Conductors, Insulators and the Switch
concepts.definition: Materials differ at carrying current: metals conduct and light the bulb, while plastic, rubber and cloth block it as insulators; a switch uses this fact, opening and closing the metal path at will.
concepts.key_idea: Conduction decides design: wires of conductors, covers of insulators, and a switch to command the loop.
